data.title: Anchor
data.tagline: Jump to a named section on the same long page
data.description: Anchor navigation helps people scan and jump within documentation, policies, and other long pages. Keep section labels aligned with headings and update the active item as the page scrolls. It does not replace navigation between separate pages.

use: A page with several clearly named sections
avoid: Use anchors for content on different pages
List headings that do not exist
Cover the target heading with a sticky header
Add anchor navigation to a page too short to need it

lessonPractice.title: A long installation guide has Environment, Install, Configure, and Troubleshoot sections. Users need fast jumps and awareness of the current section. How should it navigate?

options.label: Create an in-page table of contents linked to anchors and highlight the current section on scroll
options.feedback: Anchors locate content within the same page, while highlighting keeps the directory synchronized with reading position.

options.label: Turn the four sections into tabs and unmount every section except the selected one
options.feedback: Tabs split a continuous document into exclusive states, preventing natural reading and addressable in-page locations.

options.label: Only add Back to top after each section and make users find the next section again
options.feedback: Returning to the top does not directly reach a target or communicate current position, so navigation remains costly.

data.agentPrompt: Generate an in-page table of contents with stable section anchors and highlight the active section while scrolling. Account for the fixed header offset and verify that a copied anchor URL lands on the correct heading.
